title: add-prefill-cost-cartographer-and-tenant-autoscaler-hooks
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Large tenants show variable prefill characteristics that drive unit economics for short-lived sessions. Our existing defaults are conservative and leave money on the table for steady workloads, but can overcommit for spiky tenants. This PR introduces the "Cost Cartographer" — a tenant-aware prefill profile curator — and a small set of autoscaler hooks that allow reserved pool sizing to be adjusted based on simulated cost/latency trade-offs.

Motivation: provide an automated, safe path to tighter batching, smarter prefill (sparse/compact), and quantization profiles tuned per-tenant workload shape without manual ops changes.

Goals: 1) Surface tenant prefill profiles derived from production traces and local simulator dry-run. 2) Provide a gated autoscaler hook that recommends reserved pool adjustments and compact quant profiles. 3) Integrate telemetry so SRE/Cost teams can validate before rollout.

What changed (high level):
- New service: prefill-cost-cartographer (go) that computes tenant profiles from traces and outputs JSON profiles into config-store.
- Simulator: lightweight prefill-sim (python) with dry-run mode that predicts per-token cost and 99th p50 latency under candidate profiles.
- Autoscaler hooks: a new hook interface in dedicated/autoscaler to accept profile proposals and run safety checks (latency SLO regressions, quality loss thresholds).
- Runtime: small runtime adapter to accept tenant profile at request time and apply compact prefill/kv-cache hints.
- Telemetry: new dashboards/metrics and a rollout audit trail (prefill.cartographer.decisions).

Checklist (automated & manual):
- [x] Trace ingestion + tenant grouping (prefill-cost-cartographer)
- [x] Simulator implementation + unit tests (prefill-sim)
- [x] Autoscaler hook wire-up + safety gate (loss-based threshold)
- [x] Runtime adapter + integration tests
- [x] End-to-end dry-run against canary tenant dataset
- [x] Telemetry dashboards + alerting rules added (SLO regressions)
- [x] Docs: short how-to for operators and runbook notes

Compatibility & safety: The cartographer's proposals are advisory only. The autoscaler hook rejects proposals that fail the loss/latency safety gate. The simulator supports a 'conservative_multiplier' and rollback TTL so any accidental regressions are automatically reversed.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests added across Go/Python modules.
- Integration tests run in CI against a synthetic tenant trace set.
- Load-tested in perf-lab with 3 tenant shapes: steady, bursty, and long-context.

Observed: 6-12% token cost savings for steady workloads with <1% p99 latency change when compact prefill was used.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag.
2) Dry-run mode: proposals logged but not applied for 48h.
3) Canary: enable apply for 5 low-risk tenants.
4) Gradual escalation with telemetry-driven gating.

Related: ENG-2208 (prefill profiling), ENG-2219 (autoscaler hooks), SUP-1421 (support ticket tracking tenant cost concerns).

Follow-ups:
- Add automated A/B prompt-eval harness to quantify quality deltas per-tenant.
- Surface an API for customers to opt-out of tenant-level compression.
- Implement a compact-quant tier selector (future PR).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can the simulator surface per-token variance (stddev) so the safety gate can be less brittle?

Leah Morrison: Suggest adding a short-circuit if the proposal reduces memory below the model's kv cache minimum — otherwise we'll OOM on long-context requests.
Maya Chen: Added check in runtime adapter and autoscaler hook to enforce kv cache floor; added unit tests (commit c3f9a10).
Diego Ramos: CI flake on linux-py39, looks like a test race in sim fixtures; fixed by ensuring deterministic ordering (commit f6c9d43).

release_notes: Introduce tenant-aware prefill cost cartographer and autoscaler hooks. Adds advisory profiling, a simulator dry-run mode, runtime adapter for compact prefill hints, and telemetry. Feature is behind a feature flag and rolled out to canary tenants. Expected cost savings for steady tenants: 6-12% with conservative safety gating.
